text:
morgan: FYI — after the 1.30 rolling upgrade for eu-west cluster the cluster-autoscaler stopped scaling our GPU nodepool. Pods are pending on gpu nodes and the autoscaler log shows no matches for the nodepool selector.

infra-bot: upgrade-notify: cluster/eu-west updated to v1.30.0 at 2026-03-17T11:59:47Z

sylvia: ugh, same as the test cluster? any errors in the autoscaler logs?

morgan: here's the snippet from autoscaler: 
```
I0317 12:02:11.123456 1 scale.go:342] No nodegroup matches ProvisionerRef: apiVersion "v1alpha1" not found
I0317 12:02:11.123457 1 scale.go:345] fallback: trying label-based match for nodepool
I0317 12:02:11.123458 1 scale.go:346] no matching node labels found for selector: nodepool.k8s.redwood/v1alpha1.nodePoolSelector
```

morgan: and kubectl showing the CRD on the cluster: 
```
$ kubectl get nodepools -o yaml -n redwood-system
apiVersion: nodepools.redwood.com/v1beta2
items:
- metadata:
    name: gpu-pool-eu
  spec:
    selector: 
      matchLabels:
        redwood.com/gpu: "true"
    provisionerRef:
      apiVersion: nodepools.redwood.com/v1
      kind: NodePool
      name: gpu-pool-eu
```

morgan: looks like the provisionerRef/apiVersion canonicalization changed in 1.30 and our autoscaler is still expecting v1alpha1/v1beta1 form so it rejects the ref.

raj: I saw something similar on staging — kube 1.30 flattens CRD group/version in the controller runtime and we missed the newer apiVersion alias. Quick mitigation is to fallback to label matching (we already have the label on the pool).

raj: I pushed a small hotfix that makes the autoscaler accept multiple apiVersion aliases and tries label-only fallback earlier: https://github.com/redwood-infra/autoscaler/pull/324 (wip). Can someone test on eu-west staging?

ops-oncall: if this is hitting production and blocking customers, we should consider pausing further upgrades and apply the hotfix. Is there a safe rollback for 1.30?

morgan: Production is affected for a handful of inference jobs; not full outage but backlog increasing. We can patch autoscaler without rolling back kube.

raj: test patch applied to the autoscaler deployment in eu-west-staging and observed scaling resume: 
```
I0317 12:25:02.887654 1 scale.go:360] matched nodepool gpu-pool-eu via labels: redwood.com/gpu=true
I0317 12:25:02.887660 1 scale.go:412] autoscaling: scheduling 2 extra nodes for pending-gpu-workload
```

sylvia: nice. can we get a tiny release and a canary rollout for prod? Also add a unit test for apiVersion alias matching.

raj: yes — creating a 0.9.7-hotfix tag and doing a canary in prod (one autoscaler pod) before full rollout. PR updated with tests.

infra-bot: deploy: autoscaler 0.9.7-hotfix canary deployed to cluster/eu-west at 2026-03-17T12:40:10Z by @raj

ops-oncall: monitoring whether backlog drains; please keep me posted. If scaling doesn't resume fully after canary, we can revert upgrade or force nodepool scale via terraform.

morgan: after canary the backlog started clearing, and gpu nodes spinning up again. Thanks @raj.

raj: I'll follow up with a small postmortem and include the root cause: CRD apiVersion alias change + selector key mismatch. Plan: broaden apiVersion matching, add label fallback, and include compatibility note in upgrade playbook.

sylvia: add a doc item to eng-infra runbook: "Kubernetes upgrade checklist — CRD aliasing + autoscaler compatibility".

morgan: assigning follow-ups: @raj push full rollout, @sylvia update runbook, @ops-oncall monitor for 24h.

ops-oncall: ack.
